did_you_know.text: Did you know? Merodach-baladan, king of Babylon, sent Hezekiah letters and a gift after hearing that Hezekiah had been ill and had recovered.
Did you know? Hezekiah showed the Babylonian envoys all his treasures: silver, gold, spices, precious oil, his household articles, and everything found in his treasuries.
Did you know? The passage emphasizes that Hezekiah hid nothing from the envoys of all that was in his palace and throughout his kingdom.
Did you know? Isaiah asked Hezekiah who the men were and where they had come from, and Hezekiah replied that they had come from a distant land—from Babylon.
Did you know? When Isaiah asked what the envoys had seen in his palace, Hezekiah admitted that he had shown them everything in his treasuries.
Did you know? Before announcing what would happen in the future, Isaiah began by saying to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the LORD of Hosts.”
Did you know? Isaiah prophesied that all the treasures in Hezekiah’s palace and everything his ancestors had stored up to that day would be carried off to Babylon, and that nothing would be left.
Did you know? The prophecy also included Hezekiah’s descendants: his sons would be taken away and become eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
Did you know? Hezekiah accepted the prophetic message and said that it was good, because he understood that there would be peace and truth during his lifetime.
